svg.text: Nodes hold descriptors and references; variable-length key bytes live in range records appended to key blocks; nodes and key blocks are the same kind of block, taken from one pool.
and sets node capacity, at most 255 slots. Key names inside nodes are labels for readability; nodes store references, not key bytes. Logical order is shown; the slot permutation is omitted.
Tiny sizes to keep the figure readable: a page of 4 blocks, nodes of 3 slots. Pool pages are 64 KiB; the block size is fixed at compilation (RESOLVER1_BLOCK_SIZE, default 2 KiB)

a RangeRef names one record: first block, offset, begin length, end offset, end length, first-block generation. Point range [k, k\0): the record stores k\0 once; begin reads it without the final byte.
A separator can reuse the range record of its child’s first live entry; it compares only the begin. Keys are not globally deduplicated.
separator RangeRef, begin only: the same
record as the child’s first leaf entry
leaf entry: RangeRef + cv; a point range [k, k\0) references one record
PagePool: every node and every key block is one block of the same pool
freeBlocks: 5 → 6 → 7. A block released by a node can hold key records next, and the reverse; nothing is partitioned by role.
keyBlocks: K1 → K2, allocation order. Reclamation takes the oldest key block or the oldest node, whichever is older by CV, and returns it to freeBlocks.
key block: records appended in order
one block; C slots, set by the block size; not a byte-accurate layout
Structure of arrays: insertion and deletion shift the one-byte entries of order[], not the descriptors.
Internal nodes instead hold separator RangeRefs, separator CVs, child pointers and child maximum CVs.
Leaf links and lastCleanReadBatch are leaf-only fields.
